episodes.157436: Numerous thunderstorms affected the coastal waters offshore Cape Canaveral during the early morning hours. One of the storms located 25 miles east of Port Canaveral produced winds over 40 knots.
episodes.157472: With a low pressure system centered to the southwest of New Mexico and an anomalously moist air mass being transported into the state, the stage was set for another round of showers and thunderstorms across the area on May 30, 2021. Thunderstorm activity formed by the late morning hours and intensified as the day progressed. Several reports of large hail was received across central and eastern New Mexico, and a few tornadoes and landspouts were observed across the plains. The anomalously moist air mass allowed for heavy rain to fall as well, especially across south central and southeast New Mexico which received rainfall totals of three to five inches in a very short period of time. This led to flash flooding in Lincoln and Chaves counties in which several water rescues had to be performed. Widespread damage was reported as well with multiple businesses, homes, and vehicles being inundated with flood waters. Tragically, one individual in southern Lincoln County drowned while trying to cross a flooded roadway in their vehicle.
episodes.157473: A stalled low pressure system remained to the southwest of New Mexico while an anomalously moist air mass also stayed in place on May 31, 2021. With sufficient instability and shear, showers and thunderstorms developed early in the day thanks to an additional upper-level disturbance. The heavy rain that fell over south central and southeast New Mexico the previous day provided a saturated ground that was ripe for more flash flooding. Early morning storms over Chaves County produced heavy rainfall of an additional three to five inches that resulted in flash flooding from Roswell southward to Lake Arthur. The major flash flooding resulted in multiple feet of water along U.S. Highway 285 as well as low water crossings and arroyos that were breached. Heavy rain also fell in the Albuquerque area with several inches of water being reported on roadways on the west side of the metro which resulted in several stalled cars as well as flooded homes and garages.
episodes.157475: A midlevel trough lifted across western Colorado and produced scattered to numerous showers and thunderstorms. Increased instability fueled stronger thunderstorms across portions of southwest Colorado. These stronger storms produced frequent lightning, heavy rain, and large hail.
episodes.157706: Persistent low level winds out of the east brought substantial moisture to the region and contributed to severe supercell thunderstorm development as an upper level disturbance approached from the southwest. Large hail, severe wind gusts, flooding rains and tornadoes all occurred on this day. An nearly stationary outflow boundary provided strong turning in the low level wind fields that created additional wind shear which was instrumental in development of several tornadoes with the supercells that tracked near or along the boundary. A total of 13 tornadoes were confirmed in what turned out to be the highest tornado producing event of the season, although most of these were very short lived, weak, and produced little damage and/or impact. Seven tornadoes occurred in Cimarron County, mainly in the vicinity of Felt, all of which occurred over open land but were well documented by chasers. Six tornadoes occurred in Dallam and Sherman Counties, all of which were rated EF-0 or were unable to be rated due to a lack of damage indicators. Additionally, heavy rainfall occurred in many locations given the large amount of moisture in place, with flash flooding occurring in Amarillo, Canyon, and Wellington. Some locations received more than 4 inches of rainfall.
episodes.157712: Thunderstorms developed off of the Sacramento Mountains of New Mexico on the afternoon of the 30th. This activity became more widespread as it approached West Texas among stronger available instability. However, a general lack of deep layer shear prevented most of these storms from becoming severe. This thunderstorm activity eventually became very slow moving and produced heavy rainfall over a large area over Hockley County. Numerous reports of flooding were reported in Hockley County from Sundown to Levelland. A widespread area generally received over three inches of rainfall during the evening of the 30th.
episodes.157716: Strong to severe thunderstorms developed along a cold front across north-central Wisconsin during the afternoon hours. The strongest storms produced hail up to quarter size as they tracked through the region.
episodes.157717: Strong storms produced gusty winds as they tracked over the bay of Green Bay and Lake Michigan waters during the late afternoon and early evening hours.
episodes.158229: Building instability ahead of an advancing frontal boundary generated isolated severe thunderstorms over portions of western Upper Michigan on the afternoon of the 31st.
episodes.158344: A slow moving cold front interacted with a very warm and moist airmass across the region and produced very heavy rainfall mainly along and north of I20.  About 2 to 4 inches fell mainly along and north of a line from Sterling City to Brownwood and flooded several roads across the region.
episodes.158511: Strong showers and storms sparked from both the Gulf and Atlantic sea breezes produced heavy rainfall, hail, and strong winds across inland sections of South FL during the afternoon hours.
episodes.158582: A cold front approaching from the west led to the development of thunderstorms across Northwestern Wisconsin during the afternoon of May 31. While most of the storms remained below severe limits, one storm did produce hail to the size of half dollars across Price County.
episodes.158778: A broken line of thunderstorms moved across portions of western Wisconsin on May 31st. A few of these storms dropped some hail as they moved across the area. The largest reported hail was nickel sized in Urne (Buffalo County).
episodes.158779: A broken line of thunderstorms moved across portions of southeast Minnesota on May 31st. A few of these storms dropped some hail as they moved across the area. The largest reported hail was nickel sized near West Concord (Dodge County).
episodes.158794: An upper trough was over the region with abundant low-level moisture present across West Texas. A cold front was moving southward from southwest Oklahoma and there was a nearly stationary outflow boundary across Ector County from storms the previous day. Rain and thunderstorms were across the Permian Basin during the morning hours which resulted in hail across portions of the area. High instability due to clearing skies allowed for severe thunderstorms to develop across the southern Permian Basin and in Pecos County during the afternoon hours. These storms produced large hail and tornadoes. Flash flooding developed across portions of the Permian Basin during the early afternoon hours.
episodes.158882: A weakening line of thunderstorms Memorial Day morning, followed by a second line of storms that evening (which developed along an approaching cold front), led to instances of heavy rain and flooding across the region. One storm also produced minor wind damage.
episodes.158927: Showers and thunderstorms formed in the vicinity of a stationary front and produced isolated heavy rain resulting in one flash flooding report.

Thunderstorms produced heavy rain that led to flash flooding. Marble Creek sent over a foot of water over the roadway at the 6700 block of Colton-Bluff Springs Rd. in southern Austin.

A trained spotter near Milnesand reported hailstones ranging from the size of nickels to quarters from a severe thunderstorm tracking eastward through the area.
A storm chaser reported hail up to quarter size about five miles west of Morton. Additionally, trees were blown down just east of the location of the hail.

Widespread thunderstorms over the western and southwestern South Plains produced heavy rainfall over a large area. Numerous reports of flooding were received in Hockley County with multiple roads underwater. Widespread rain totals of up to three inches were common over the flooded areas.

Multiple trained spotters reported flash flooding along U.S. Highway 285 near Midway with an estimated three to four feet of water over the roadway. Several people were stranded along the highway and were waiting on top of their vehicles to be rescued. Several water rescues had to be conducted at U.S. Highway 285 and Orchard Park Road. Multiple homes were inundated as well with flood waters, and one woman had to be rescued via a kayak. No injuries were reported. The extent of the damages is unknown, and damages are roughly estimated for the multiple businesses, homes, and vehicles inundated with flood waters.
Street flooding reported on South Coulter near Hollywood Road construction zones.

events.narrative: NOAA Buoy 41009, located 25 miles offshore Port Canaveral, recorded a peak wind of 41 knots as a strong thunderstorm crossed the platform.

Thunderstorms producing heavy rain resulted in major flash flooding across southern Roswell and southern Chaves County. Heavy rainfall had fallen in the area the previous evening, and an additional 3 to 5 inches of rain during the morning of May 31st exacerbated the flash flooding. Numerous locations along U.S. Highway 285 from Lake Arthur northward into Roswell had upwards of 2 feet of water along the travel corridor while low water crossings had upwards of 4 feet of water which overfilled the banks. Multiple reports of flooding across fields, ditches, yards, and vehicles were reported. Several side roads were unpassable and had to be barricaded. A breached arroyo near the Roswell Airport also forced the closure of roads around the airport for about a week. Damages are estimated.
Fisher County Sheriff's Office reported flowing water over U.S. Highway 180 just west of Roby.
There was a report of one inch diameter hail just southeast of L'anse along Highway US-41.  Hail accumulated up to an inch in depth.
Fisher County Sheriff's Office reported water flowing over the road on State Highway 70 just north of the Fisher County Hospital.
Fisher County Sheriff's Office reported water flowing over the road on State Highway 70 about 6 miles north of Sweetwater.
The observer reported nickel-sized hail in Paulding.

Heavy rain produced flash flooding in Odessa. As many as 27 swift water rescues were made across Odessa due to prolific flooding across the area. There were several pictures that showed abandoned cars engulfed in the flood waters. The cost of damage is a very rough estimate.
A severe thunderstorm produced large hail measured to be the size of quarters southeast of Stoner.

Heavy rain resulted in flash flooding across Odessa. There were reports of flash flooding across portions of Odessa on social media. There were pictures of water up to the top steps of home porches on Hancock Avenue. The cost of damage is a very rough estimate.

Heavy rain resulted in flash flooding in Odessa. There were pictures of flooding across the intersection of 8th Street and Muskingum Avenue. The water was high enough to move a dumpster into the middle of the intersection. The cost of damage is a very rough estimate.

Heavy rain produced flash flooding in Odessa. There was a video of a car floating down Tom Green Avenue with water several feet deep across the residential area. The cost of damage is a very rough estimate.

Heavy rain resulted in flash flooding in Odessa. There were pictures of water up to the side of cars and trucks along Walnut Street. A few vehicles were submerged up to the hood. The water was at least two to three feet deep. The cost of damage is a very rough estimate.
There was at least a couple of inches of standing water on the road near the intersection of South Clack Street and Nonesuch Road.
The County Emergency Manager measured three-quarter inch diameter hail from a thunderstorm three miles west of Ishpeming.
There was a delayed report of quarter to half-dollar sized hail from a thunderstorm near National Mine.  The hail covered the ground and dented a truck.
A severe thunderstorm produced large hail measured to be the size of pennies west-southwest of Durango. The hail accumulated on the ground.
Nickel size hail fell in Lac de Flambeau.
Penny size hail fell near Lac de Flambeau.
A trained spotter south of U.S. Highway 380 observed a landspout near Bingham. No damage was recorded.
A public report indicated flash flooding near Highway 180 in the city of Breckenridge, TX. An emergency manager also reported Gunsolus Creek was out of its banks.

Heavy rain resulted in flash flooding near Colorado City. There were pictures and video from a spotter of flash flooding ongoing along the Colorado River north northwest of Colorado City. The water was several feet deep and flowing quickly.  The water was well over the banks. No damage was reported.
Law enforcement officials reported multiple low water crossings with flowing water in Baird, and people were trapped in their vehicles.
A social media user near Golf Course and Subio in northwest Albuquerque reported nickel size hail from a severe thunderstorm moving eastward through the metro area.
A public report indicated that a sheet metal roof was lifted and trees were blown down along County Road 479 near the intersection of County Roads 570 and 571.
Quarter size hail fell in Sugar Camp.
Amateur radio reported street flooding near the Leon River in the city of Eastland, TX.
Nickel size hail fell near Three Lakes.
Multiple observers near Rio Rancho reported 1 inch hail from a severe thunderstorm moving eastward through the area.
Texas Department of Transportation reported water over the roadway on southbound U.S. Highway 180.
Texas Department of Transportation reported water over the roadway along many points on FM 1084 just outside of Albany.
A spotter observed a brief landspout near Veguita. No damage was recorded.
A trained spotter near Coors Bypass in northwest Albuquerque reported 1 inch hail from a severe thunderstorm moving eastward through the metro area.

A thunderstorm produced a tornado nineteen miles south of Fort Stockton. This tornado lasted sixteen minutes and traveled 6.3 miles to twenty-two miles south southeast of Fort Stockton. The timing and location of the tornado was estimated by both spotter reports and radar. This tornado was observed to have lifted and touched down multiple times. The tornado remained over very rural terrain on private land and did not encounter any damage indicators and was therefore rated as an EF-Unknown.
Amateur radio reported flood waters about one foot deep over FM 2214 approximately 4 miles east of Eastland, TX.
A CoCoRaHS observer near Ellison and Golf Course in northwest Albuquerque reported penny size hail from a severe thunderstorm moving eastward through the metro area.

Heavy rain from a severe thunderstorm resulted in flash flooding on the west side of Albuquerque. An estimated six inches of water on the roadways along with three inches of hail accumulation resulted in major flash flooding along Coors Boulevard and Paseo del Norte as well as Coors Boulevard and Alameda. Numerous cars were stalled along the major travel corridor in northwest Albuquerque. Farther south near Central Avenue and 52nd Street, multiple homes and garages in the neighborhood were flooded with several inches of rain and nearly six inches of hail accumulation. Damages are estimated.
Local county Sheriff reported a tornado touch down with a few power poles snapped off and downed.
Quarter size hail fell near Rhinelander.

A thunderstorm produced a tornado 21 miles south southeast of Fort Stockton and it lifted 23 miles south southeast of Fort Stockton. The tornado tracked southeast with the storm and lasted around eight minutes before wrapping around a wall cloud and becoming obscured to spotters. The path length was estimated to be 3.3 miles and since the tornado remained over private rural land with no damage reported, it was rated as an EF-Unknown.
A trained spotter estimated wind gusts to 60 mph and pea size hail at Rattlesnake Hammock Road and SR 951, just west of Collier Blvd.
Quarter size hail fell in Rhinelander.
Nickel size hail fell in Merrill.
